transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

When I get going, I tear through a ton of food really fast, way faster than I ever used to. My regular doctor got worried about my weight and blood pressure, and I had to admit to him that my eating has just gotten completely out of hand.
After these episodes of eating a lot very quickly, do you ever try to make up for it by vomiting, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising a lot?
No, I don't do any of those things like throwing up, fasting, or trying to purge. Usually, I'm just so stuffed and miserable afterward that I just sit there in the kitchen, too full to even move.
How often do these episodes happen, and have they been going on for at least 3 months?

It happens at least once or twice a week now, usually late at night when everyone else is asleep. This whole pattern has been going on for over a year, starting shortly after I stepped back from my event-planning work.
During these episodes, do you feel a loss of control, like you cannot stop eating or cannot control how much you eat?

Yes, completely. Once I start, it feels like some switch flips and I’m just shoveling food in on autopilot. Even while I’m telling myself, "George, stop, you’re done," my hands keep going back to the pan like I’m not the one in charge.
Do you feel very distressed about your binge eating or strongly influenced by your weight and body shape, even if you do not purge afterward?

I feel incredibly distressed and full of self-loathing afterward, sitting there thinking I'm ruining my health and my marriage. I've also gained so much weight that I'm too embarrassed to go to church or social events anymore because I just hate how I look.
Have you started any new medications, had any hormone or medical problems, or used substances that might be causing the overeating or weight gain?

No, I haven't started any new medications or substances, and I don't have any hormone issues that I know of. My primary doctor did note that my blood pressure has been rising and I have some nagging knee pain, but nothing else medically that would explain the overeating.
Do you ever regularly eat unusually large amounts of food when you are not physically hungry, or eat much more quickly and secretly than most people would in a similar situation?

Yes, that is exactly what happens. I'll wander into the kitchen late at night when I'm not even hungry, sometimes right after having a full dinner, and eat incredibly fast without even tasting it. I end up standing there alone, polishing off massive amounts of food that could easily feed a whole crowd.
When these eating episodes happen, do you ever have any regular behaviors to prevent weight gain afterward, such as vomiting, taking laxatives or diuretics, fasting, or exercising excessively?

No, I don't do any of those things to try and prevent weight gain. Instead, I just sit there in the quiet kitchen, feeling too stuffed to move, staring at the dirty pans and hating myself for what I did.
Have you ever had periods of eating very little or intentionally avoiding food because of fear of gaining weight, outside of these binge episodes?

No, I haven't really had times where I restricted my food or avoided eating because I was afraid of gaining weight. My struggle has always been the opposite—just overeating and completely losing control.
Have you ever had a period where you intentionally ate very little, skipped meals, or strongly restricted food because you were afraid of gaining weight?
No, I've never intentionally restricted my food, skipped meals, or fasted to try and keep from gaining weight. My issue has really just been the out-of-control eating, not trying to starve myself.

Have you ever had a period of being significantly underweight or intentionally restricting food because of fear of gaining weight, or has it always been mainly binge eating without purging or restriction?

No, I’ve never been underweight, and I have never restricted my food or tried to purge. It’s always been about these out-of-control eating episodes that started a little over a year ago, which have actually caused me to gain weight very rapidly.

Have you ever had episodes of eating much less than usual or intentionally restricting food because of fear of gaining weight, or has it always been mainly binge eating without purging or restriction?

It has always been mainly the out-of-control binge eating. I have never forced myself to throw up or intentionally starved myself to lose weight, even though I'm very unhappy about how much weight I've gained. My struggle is purely with those late-night episodes where I lose all control and eat massive amounts of food.
Have you ever had times when the binge eating was followed by any compensatory behavior, like vomiting, laxative use, fasting, or exercising to make up for it?
No, I've never done anything like that to make up for it. After those episodes, I just sit there feeling incredibly stuffed, miserable, and too heavy to even move.
Just to confirm, after these binge episodes, do you ever do anything to prevent weight gain, such as vomiting, using laxatives or diuretics, fasting, or exercising excessively?

No, I definitely don't do any of that—no throwing up, laxatives, fasting, or heavy exercise. I'm usually just so incredibly full and miserable afterward that I can't do much of anything besides sit there.
Have you ever had any periods of purging, fasting, or exercising excessively to try to prevent weight gain after eating, even if it was only occasionally?

No, I've never done any of that, not even occasionally. Honestly, after those episodes, I just feel way too sluggish and down on myself to even think about exercising or doing anything else to make up for it.

Have you ever had a period of being significantly underweight or intentionally restricting food because of fear of gaining weight, or has it always been mainly binge eating without purging or restriction?

No, I have never been underweight or restricted my food, and I've never tried to purge either. My struggles have really just been with this recent pattern of out-of-control overeating. It's always been about losing control during those late-night episodes.
Have you ever intentionally tried to lose weight by eating much less, skipping meals, or following strict diet rules because you were afraid of gaining weight?
No, I haven't really tried strict dieting or skipping meals to lose weight. My main struggle has always been the overeating and losing control, rather than trying to restrict what I eat.
Do you ever have times when you eat very large amounts of food without feeling out of control, or is the loss of control always present during these episodes?

The loss of control is always there during those episodes. Once I start eating, it feels like a switch flips and I go on autopilot, with my hands just reaching for food even when I'm telling myself to stop.
When these episodes happen, do you eat an unusually large amount of food in a short period of time, and do you feel a clear loss of control while it’s happening?

Yes, absolutely. I can polish off a whole church-potluck-sized spread of wings, sliders, and mac and cheese by myself in just ten or fifteen minutes. While I'm doing it, it feels like a switch flips and I go on autopilot, with my hands reaching for more food even as I'm mentally telling myself to stop.
Have you ever had periods where you purposely ate very little, skipped meals, or followed strict diet rules to control your weight, even if you did not vomit or purge afterward?

No, I haven't really tried strict dieting, skipping meals, or restricting my food intake in that way. My main issue has just been the out-of-control overeating, rather than trying to limit what I eat.
Have you ever had a period of trying to lose weight by severely restricting food, skipping meals, or following strict diet rules because you were afraid of gaining weight?
No, I haven't really tried strict dieting, skipping meals, or severe food restriction. It's always just been about the out-of-control eating episodes rather than trying to restrict my food.

Have you ever had a time when you were significantly underweight or were intentionally restricting food because you were afraid of gaining weight, even if that was before these binge episodes started?

No, I've never really struggled with being underweight or intentionally restricted my food intake in that way. My issues have always been on the opposite side of the spectrum, where I just can't seem to stop eating once I start.

Have you ever had a time when you were significantly underweight, or have you ever intentionally restricted your food because you were afraid of gaining weight? This helps distinguish binge-eating disorder from other eating disorders.
No, I have never been underweight, and I’ve never intentionally restricted my food or starved myself to keep from gaining weight. For me, it has always just been about the out-of-control overeating.
Have you ever had any periods of significant weight loss, very low body weight, or strong fear of gaining weight that led you to restrict food, even if that was before the binge eating started?
No, I've never had any periods of significant weight loss or a very low body weight. My struggles have really just been with weight gain and overeating, rather than restricting my food.
Do you feel that your self-worth is strongly tied to your weight or body shape, or that you are overly focused on them?

I'm not really sure, as I haven't really thought about my self-worth in those exact terms. I do know that I feel incredibly embarrassed about my recent weight gain, which makes me want to hide away from people.
Do you find that your self-worth is strongly tied to your weight or body shape, or that you spend a lot of time worrying about them?

I'm not entirely sure how to describe that feeling, or if my overall self-worth is tied to my shape. I just know I feel incredibly embarrassed about my recent weight gain and how I look, which has even made me avoid going to church lately.
Do you spend a lot of time thinking about your weight or body shape, or feel that your self-worth depends heavily on how you look?

While I feel incredibly self-conscious and embarrassed about my recent weight gain—even avoiding social events because of how I look—I'm not sure I'd say my entire self-worth depends on my appearance. I don't really constantly obsess over my body shape, I'm just really unhappy and frustrated with how out of hand things have gotten.
Do you spend a lot of time thinking about your weight or body shape, or feel that your self-worth depends heavily on how you look?

Like I mentioned, I'm really not sure if my entire self-worth depends on my appearance, as I haven't thought about it in those terms. I just know that I feel incredibly embarrassed about my recent weight gain and how I look right now.
Do you spend a lot of time thinking about your weight or body shape, or feel that your self-worth depends heavily on how you look?

I'm still not sure if I would say my entire self-worth depends on my appearance, and I don't really spend a lot of time obsessing over my body shape. I just feel incredibly embarrassed about my recent rapid weight gain, which has even made me avoid church and other social gatherings because of how I look.
Do you feel that your self-worth is strongly tied to your weight or body shape, or do you spend a lot of time thinking about how your body looks?

I don't really know if my entire self-worth is tied to my shape, but the shame about my physical appearance and losing control makes me want to hide from people. I'm just extremely embarrassed about my recent weight gain and how I look, which is why I've been avoiding church gatherings and event gigs.
